name: Chicken & Spinach Breakfast Pot
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, diced small
1 tbsp olive oil, for the pot
instructions: Dice the chicken small so it finishes with the eggs. Oil the slow cooker insert well.
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with garlic powder, pepper, and oregano. Stir in spinach, pepper, onion, and chicken.
Pour into the pot. Cook on LOW only. HIGH makes the eggs weep.
Check at 2.5 hours. The center should be just set and the chicken at 165°F.
Rest 10 minutes, then cut into 6 containers.
doneWhen: Center set, chicken 165°F. No pink in the meat.
tips: Fridge 3 days. Reheat covered so the eggs stay tender. No salt in the pot; pepper and oregano carry it.

name: Herb Chicken with Soft Eggs
ingredients: 2 cups spinach or zucchini, to warm at the end
instructions: Set the bath to 150°F (66°C). Season chicken with pepper, thyme, garlic powder, and lemon zest. Add the oil.
Seal with a vacuum sealer or the water-displacement method. Cook 1.5–2 hours, until the thickest piece is pasteurized and juicy.
Pull the chicken. Raise the bath to 167°F (75°C). Lower in the eggs for 13 minutes, then an ice bath.
Slice the chicken. Peel the eggs. Warm the greens in a dry pan with pepper and a squeeze of the lemon you zested.
Pack one portion of chicken, one egg, and greens.
doneWhen: Chicken opaque and 150°F+ through the center after the full time. Eggs peeled clean.
tips: Juice goes on after cooking, not in the bag, so the chicken stays firm. Fridge 3 days.

name: Lemon Herb Chicken with Broccoli
instructions: Put chicken, onion, garlic, broth, lemon juice, herbs, pepper, and garlic powder in the slow cooker.
Cook on LOW 3–4 hours. Start checking at 3 hours. Pull when the thickest piece is 165°F. Longer than that dries the breast.
Add broccoli for the last 30–40 minutes so it stays bright.
Slice or shred the chicken into the juices. Portion with the broccoli.
doneWhen: Chicken 165°F, broccoli tender-crisp, juices still thin and lemony.
tips: Use the juices as the sauce. Freeze portions up to 2 months. Cauliflower works if broccoli isn't around.

name: Chicken Salad, Yogurt & Dill
ingredients: 1 tsp Dijon mustard (optional; it adds a little sodium)
instructions: Season chicken with pepper, garlic powder, dill, and lemon zest. Seal and cook at 150°F for 1.5–2 hours.
Ice-bath the bags 10 minutes so the chicken stays shreddable, not steamy.
Chop or shred. Fold in yogurt, celery, lemon juice, and mustard if you use it.
Pack over a big pile of lettuce. Do not add salt.
doneWhen: Chicken fully opaque, salad cold and creamy, not watery.
tips: The yogurt dressing is the sodium watch-out if you add mustard. Skip mustard to stay lower. Fridge 3 days.

name: Garlic Chicken & Zucchini
instructions: Add chicken, broth, garlic, pepper, paprika, rosemary, and onion.
Cook on LOW 3–4 hours, until the chicken hits 165°F.
Stir in zucchini and vinegar for the last 30 minutes.
Slice the chicken and spoon the garlicky juices over each portion.
doneWhen: Chicken 165°F, zucchini soft but not mush, garlic fragrant.
tips: Paprika and vinegar stand in for salt. Freeze the chicken; add fresh zucchini when you reheat if you want more bite.

name: Lemon Thyme Chicken Breast
ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, about 6 oz each
Steamed broccoli or green beans, for serving
instructions: Set the bath to 150°F. For a firmer, more traditional texture, use 156°F.
Season each breast with pepper, thyme, garlic, zest, and oil. Seal.
Cook 1.5 hours for a 1-inch breast, up to 2.5 hours if thicker. Do not go past 4 hours or the texture turns soft.
Optional: pat dry and sear 30–45 seconds a side in a hot pan for color. Squeeze lemon on after.
Slice and pack with a large serving of the vegetable.
doneWhen: Opaque edge to edge, juices clear, thickest point at the bath temperature.
tips: Cook the week's breasts in one bath. Fridge 3–4 days, or freeze the sealed bags up to 2 months.

name: Turkey Pepper Breakfast Bake
ingredients: 1 lb lean ground turkey (93% or leaner)
instructions: Brown the turkey in a skillet with pepper, paprika, sage, and garlic powder. Drain any fat. Let it cool a few minutes.
Whisk the eggs and egg whites. Stir in turkey, pepper, onion, and spinach.
Oil the slow cooker. Cook on LOW 3–3.5 hours until the center is set and the turkey is 165°F.
Rest, then portion into 6 containers.
doneWhen: Egg center set, turkey 165°F, no pink remaining.
tips: Browning first keeps the pot from watering out. Fridge 3 days.

name: Turkey Patties & Jammy Eggs
instructions: Mix turkey with pepper, garlic powder, sage, and paprika. Form 4 thin patties and stack them in a bag with a little space, or seal in one flat layer.
Cook at 160°F (71°C) for 1.5 hours so the ground poultry is pasteurized.
Raise the bath to 167°F and cook the eggs 13 minutes. Ice-bath both.
Pack a patty, an egg, and peppers. A splash of hot sauce is optional and usually low sodium if you check the label.
doneWhen: Patties 160°F through the center for the full time, eggs just set.
tips: Thin patties heat more evenly than a thick log. Fridge 3 days.

name: Turkey & Cabbage Pot
instructions: Brown the turkey in a skillet and drain. This step is worth it.
Add turkey, cabbage, onion, garlic, broth, paprika, pepper, and thyme to the slow cooker.
Cook on LOW 3.5–4.5 hours, until cabbage is tender and turkey is 165°F.
Stir in the vinegar at the end. Portion.
doneWhen: Cabbage soft, turkey 165°F, broth reduced but not dry.
tips: A big volume meal. Freeze well. Vinegar at the end replaces salt.

name: Lemon Herb Turkey Meatballs
ingredients: 1/4 cup almond flour or crushed pork rinds
instructions: Mix turkey, egg, almond flour, pepper, garlic powder, oregano, zest, and parsley. Roll 16 meatballs.
Seal in a single layer. Cook at 160°F for 1.5–2 hours.
Warm a cup of no-salt tomato passata with extra oregano. Spoon over meatballs.
Serve with a large salad or zucchini noodles.
doneWhen: Center of a meatball 160°F and held for the cook time.
tips: Passata is usually lower sodium than jarred sauce. Read the label anyway. Fridge 3 days, freezer 2 months.

name: No-Bean Turkey Chili
instructions: Brown the turkey with onion and garlic. Drain. Move to the slow cooker.
Add pepper, tomatoes, broth, chili powder, cumin, paprika, and black pepper.
Cook on LOW 4–5 hours. Turkey should be 165°F and the chili thick, not soupy.
Finish with lime juice. Top with extra raw pepper or a spoon of plain yogurt if you want.
doneWhen: Thick enough to mound, turkey fully cooked, lime bright at the end.
tips: No beans keeps the carbs down. Freeze in flat bags. Cumin and lime do the work salt usually does.

name: Paprika Turkey Cutlets
ingredients: 4 cups zucchini noodles or roasted peppers
instructions: If cutlets are thicker than 1 inch, pound them even. Season with pepper, paprika, garlic powder, oregano, and oil.
Seal and cook at 150°F for 2 hours. Whole-muscle turkey breast pasteurizes at this time and temp.
Optional 30-second sear. Splash with vinegar.
Pack with a large scoop of zucchini or peppers.
doneWhen: Cutlets opaque, 150°F through, paprika fragrant not bitter.
tips: Don't use ground turkey at 150°F. This recipe is whole muscle only. Fridge 3 days.

name: Beef & Mushroom Egg Hash
ingredients: 1 lb lean ground beef (93% or leaner)
instructions: Brown the beef with mushrooms, onion, pepper, garlic powder, thyme, and paprika. Drain the fat.
Whisk eggs and egg whites, then fold in the beef mixture and spinach.
Oil the pot. Cook on LOW 3–3.5 hours until set. Beef should be fully browned from the skillet step and the egg at 160°F+.
Rest and cut 6 portions.
doneWhen: Eggs set in the center, no pink beef, mushrooms soft.
tips: Mushrooms bring savor without salt. Fridge 3 days.

name: Steak Bites & Eggs
time: 134°F for 2 hours, then a hard sear
ingredients: 1.25 lb lean sirloin, cut in 1-inch cubes
instructions: Season the sirloin with pepper, garlic powder, and rosemary. Seal.
Cook at 134°F (57°C) for 2 hours for medium-rare whole-muscle beef. Use 140°F if you want it medium.
Pat very dry. Sear hard in a hot pan, 30–45 seconds, so the outside browns without overcooking.
In the same pan, wilt spinach. Fry or sous-vide the eggs at 167°F for 13 minutes in a second round.
Pack steak, egg, and spinach.
doneWhen: Steak seared, pink only if you chose 134°F, eggs set.
tips: Whole muscle only. Do not use this time and temp for ground beef. Fridge 3 days.

name: Pepper Beef, No Salt
ingredients: 2 lb top round or sirloin tip, cubed
instructions: Add beef, onion, garlic, broth, half the vinegar, paprika, pepper, oregano, and onion powder.
Cook on LOW 6–7 hours until the beef is fork-tender. Lean beef will not shred like chuck; slice it.
Stir in peppers for the last 45 minutes.
Finish with the rest of the vinegar. Spoon the juices over each box.
doneWhen: Beef tender when sliced, peppers soft, juices reduced.
tips: Top round stays leaner than chuck. Freeze well. Great over cauliflower rice.

name: Sirloin over Herb Salad
ingredients: 1.5 lb sirloin steak, about 1.5 inches thick
instructions: Season the steak with pepper, garlic powder, and thyme. Seal.
Cook at 134°F for 2–3 hours, or 140°F for medium.
Pat dry and sear 45 seconds a side. Rest 5 minutes. Slice thin against the grain.
Toss greens, cucumber, and herbs with lemon juice and oil. No salt. Lay the steak on top cold or warm.
doneWhen: Even color edge to edge, a real crust, salad still crisp.
tips: Slice only when you pack or eat so the meat stays juicy. Fridge 3 days.

name: Round Roast & Cauliflower
ingredients: 2.5 lb eye of round or top round
1 tbsp tomato paste, no salt added
instructions: Rub the roast with pepper, paprika, and rosemary. Put it in with onion, garlic, broth, and tomato paste.
Cook on LOW 7–8 hours. Lean roasts need the long cook to soften, and they slice better than they shred.
Add cauliflower for the last 60–75 minutes.
Rest the meat 10 minutes, slice thin against the grain, and stir balsamic into the juices.
doneWhen: Slice falls apart under a fork at the edge, center still moist, cauliflower tender.
tips: Eye of round is the lean pick. Don't swap in a fatty chuck if you are watching calories. Freezes well.

name: Rosemary Garlic Sirloin
ingredients: 1.5 lb sirloin or top round steak
instructions: Season steak with garlic, rosemary, pepper, and oil. Seal.
Cook at 134°F for 2–4 hours. Go longer only for tougher round; sirloin is best closer to 2 hours.
Sear in a ripping-hot pan, 45 seconds a side. Rest, then slice against the grain.
Steam or roast the vegetable with pepper. Splash balsamic on the meat after searing.
doneWhen: Even medium-rare or your chosen doneness, dark crust, asparagus still green.
tips: A 1-minute sear is plenty. Longer and you lose the point of the bath. Fridge 3 days.

name: Pork & Greens Breakfast Bake
instructions: Toss pork with pepper, sage, garlic powder, and mustard. Brown quickly in a skillet so the outside isn't raw going into eggs, then let it cool.
Whisk eggs and egg whites with the greens and onion. Fold in the pork.
Oil the pot. Cook on LOW 3–3.5 hours until the egg is set and the pork pieces are 145°F and no longer pink.
Rest and portion.
doneWhen: Eggs set, pork opaque and 145°F.
tips: Dry mustard adds bite without a salty jar of prepared mustard. Fridge 3 days.

name: Tenderloin Strips & Eggs
instructions: Season the tenderloin with pepper, sage, garlic powder, and zest. Seal whole.
Cook at 140°F (60°C) for 1.5–2.5 hours. That is a juicy, fully cooked tenderloin.
Sear 30 seconds a side. Slice. Cook eggs at 167°F for 13 minutes, or fry them.
Pack slices, an egg, and peppers.
doneWhen: Pork 140°F through after the full time, faint blush is normal and safe for whole tenderloin.
tips: A faint pink center at 140°F is expected, not undercooked. Fridge 3 days.

name: Pork Tenderloin & Cabbage
ingredients: 1 tsp caraway seeds or dried thyme
instructions: Season the tenderloin with pepper, garlic powder, and paprika.
Put cabbage and onion in the pot, then the pork, broth, and caraway or thyme.
Cook on HIGH 2–2.5 hours. Start checking at 2 hours. Pull at 145°F. LOW for 8 hours will chalk a tenderloin.
Rest 5 minutes, slice, and stir vinegar into the cabbage.
doneWhen: Pork 145°F in the center, cabbage tender, still a little broth in the pot.
tips: This is a short cook on purpose. Set a timer. Fridge 3 days. Freeze the pork; cabbage is better fresh.

name: Lemon Fennel Pork
instructions: Season pork with pepper, fennel, garlic powder, and zest. Seal.
Cook at 140°F for 2 hours.
Sear briefly. Slice thin.
Toss cabbage with lemon juice, oil, and pepper. Serve the pork on the slaw.
doneWhen: Pork 140°F, seared outside, slaw still crunchy.
tips: Fennel seed tastes savory, not sweet. No apple in this one, so the carbs stay low. Fridge 3 days.

name: Rosemary Garlic Tenderloin
instructions: Cut small slits in the pork and tuck in garlic. Rub with rosemary, pepper, and paprika.
Add onion and broth. Cook on HIGH 2–2.5 hours. Pull at 145°F.
Add zucchini for the last 30 minutes if the pork isn't done yet, or steam it separately if the pork finishes first.
Rest, slice, and splash with vinegar and the pot juices.
doneWhen: 145°F in the thickest part, zucchini just tender.
tips: Tenderloin is not a shoulder. If you only have all day, cook something else. Fridge 3 days.

name: Pepper Thyme Tenderloin
instructions: Rub pork with pepper, thyme, garlic powder, and oil. Seal.
Cook at 140°F for 2–3 hours.
Pat dry and sear until the outside is browned, about 45 seconds a side.
Slice. Steam the vegetable. Finish with parsley and lemon.
doneWhen: 140°F through, browned edges, broccoli bright.
tips: Batch two tenderloins in the same bath if they fit in one layer of bags. Fridge 3–4 days.

name: Salmon & Egg Breakfast Cups
ingredients: 12 oz salmon fillet, skin off, in 4 pieces
instructions: This is a short cook. Do not leave salmon in a slow cooker for hours.
Oil the pot. Lay in spinach, then salmon. Season with dill, pepper, and zest.
Crack an egg over each piece, or whisk the eggs and pour them around the fish.
Cook on LOW 60–80 minutes. Salmon should flake and reach 145°F. Eggs should be set.
Lift portions out gently.
doneWhen: Salmon flakes and is 145°F, egg fully set.
tips: Check at 60 minutes. Overcooked salmon goes chalky fast. Fridge 2 days. Don't freeze the eggs.

name: Dill Salmon & Soft Eggs
ingredients: 1 lb salmon fillet, skin on or off
instructions: Season salmon with dill, pepper, zest, and oil. Seal in a flat bag.
Cook at 130°F (54°C) for 45 minutes. Raise to 140°F for 40 minutes if you want it fully firm.
Ice-bath 5 minutes if you are packing it cold.
Cook eggs at 167°F for 13 minutes. Serve with cucumber tossed in lemon and dill.
doneWhen: Salmon just-set and flaky, or firmer if you used 140°F.
tips: Use fish you'd trust fresh. 130°F is a quality cook, not a raw one, but 140°F is the cautious choice. Fridge 2 days.

name: Lemon Dill Salmon
instructions: Lay lemon and garlic in the pot. Add broth. Set the salmon on top. Season with dill and pepper.
Cook on LOW. Check at 45 minutes. Pull when it flakes and the center is 145°F, usually by 70 minutes.
Steam the vegetables on the stove while it cooks. The slow cooker will overdo them if they go in early.
Portion salmon with a lemon slice and a big pile of vegetables.
doneWhen: Flakes under a fork, 145°F in the center, still moist.
tips: Set a timer. This is not an all-day pot. Fridge 2 days. Better not frozen after cooking.

name: Herb Salmon Salad Bowls
time: 125°F for 40 minutes, or 140°F to be firm
instructions: Season salmon with dill, pepper, and zest. Seal flat.
Cook at 125°F for 40–45 minutes for silky salmon, or 140°F for 35–40 minutes for a firmer, more traditional fillet.
Chill. Flake.
Stir yogurt with lemon juice, oil, and pepper. Dress the greens and cucumber. Top with salmon.
doneWhen: Salmon flakes into moist pieces, greens still crisp, dressing thick.
tips: Pack dressing on the side so the greens last until lunch. Fridge 2 days.

name: Tomato Herb Salmon
ingredients: Handful of fresh basil or parsley
instructions: Stir tomatoes, garlic, oregano, pepper, and paprika. Spread half in the pot.
Lay in the salmon. Spoon the rest of the tomato over it. Tuck zucchini around the sides.
Cook on LOW 50–75 minutes, until salmon is 145°F and flakes.
Top with herbs. Don't add cheese or salt.
doneWhen: Salmon 145°F, tomato thick, zucchini tender.
tips: No-salt tomatoes are the whole trick. Regular canned tomatoes can blow the sodium budget. Fridge 2 days.

name: Lemon Pepper Salmon
ingredients: Lemon juice and parsley, to finish
instructions: Season each portion with pepper, garlic powder, zest, and a touch of oil. Seal in one layer.
Cook at 130°F for 45 minutes, or 140°F for 35 minutes if you want it firmer.
Roast or steam the asparagus with pepper while the bath runs.
Open the bags, spoon the juices over the fish, and finish with lemon juice and parsley.
doneWhen: Salmon flakes, center matches the bath, asparagus still has snap.
tips: Leave the skin on in the bag if you like it; peel it off when plating if you don't. Fridge 2 days.

name: High-Protein Veggie Egg Casserole
ingredients: Cooking spray or 1 tsp olive oil
instructions: Grease the insert well, including the sides.
Whisk eggs, egg whites, yogurt, garlic powder, pepper, and paprika. Stir in spinach, pepper, and onion.
Cook on LOW 3–4 hours until set and at least 160°F in the center. HIGH makes it weep.
Rest 10 minutes. Cut into 4.
doneWhen: Center 160°F and no liquid egg left.
tips: Yogurt and whites carry the protein without a salty cheese. Carton egg whites vary in sodium, so check the label. Fridge 4 days.

name: Soft Eggs with Herbed Yogurt
instructions: Set the bath to 167°F (75°C). Cook the eggs 13–15 minutes, then an ice bath. Peel.
Stir the yogurt with herbs, pepper, and lemon zest. No salt.
Plate 3 eggs, 1 cup of the yogurt, and a pile of spinach.
doneWhen: Whites set, yogurt cold and herbed, spinach wilted.
tips: For jammy yolks, cook the eggs at 145°F for 45 minutes instead. Peeled eggs keep 2–3 days. The yogurt is the protein, so don't skip it.

name: High-Protein Pepper Egg Loaf
instructions: Oil the pot. Whisk eggs, egg whites, yogurt, oregano, pepper, and garlic powder.
Fold in spinach, bell pepper, and onion.
Cook on LOW 3–4 hours to 160°F in the center.
Cool before slicing into 4. Pack with a salad.
doneWhen: 160°F center, slices clean after a short rest.
tips: Fridge 4 days. A side salad adds volume without adding much else.

name: Jammy Eggs on a Yogurt Salad
instructions: Cook eggs at 167°F for 13 minutes. Ice bath and peel. Halve them.
Stir yogurt with lemon or vinegar, oregano, and pepper.
Each box gets a big pile of greens and cucumber, 3/4 cup yogurt, and 3 eggs.
Keep the yogurt separate until you eat so the greens stay crisp.
doneWhen: Eggs peeled, yogurt thick, greens still crisp.
tips: Three eggs plus yogurt is the meal. The salad is there so you can eat a full plate. Fridge: eggs 3 days, undressed greens 3 days.

name: High-Protein Mushroom Egg Bake
instructions: Soften mushrooms, onion, and garlic in a skillet with thyme and pepper. Cool slightly.
Whisk eggs, egg whites, and yogurt. Stir in the mushroom mix and spinach.
Oil the pot. Cook on LOW 3–4 hours to 160°F.
Rest and cut 4 portions. Add roasted zucchini if you want more on the plate.
doneWhen: 160°F, mushrooms savory, no standing liquid.
tips: Browning the mushrooms first is what makes this taste like dinner. Fridge 4 days.

name: Eggs, Yogurt, and Garlicky Greens
ingredients: Pinch of red pepper flakes, optional
instructions: Cook the eggs at 167°F for 13 minutes. Ice bath and peel.
Wilt the greens in olive oil with garlic and pepper. Finish with lemon and chili flakes if you want heat.
Each portion is 3 eggs, 3/4 cup yogurt, and a large bed of greens.
doneWhen: Eggs set, greens fully wilted and lemony, garlic soft not burnt.
tips: Greens shrink, so start with more than looks reasonable. Fridge 2 days for the greens, 3 for the eggs.

name: Berry Yogurt Bowl
ingredients: Optional: a few drops of vanilla
instructions: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Add the berries and cinnamon.
Eat it cold.
doneWhen: A full bowl, cold, with fruit on top.
tips: Strawberries keep the carbs lower than a banana. Buy plain yogurt, not a fruit cup.

name: Yogurt with Kiwi
instructions: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Add the kiwi and zest or cinnamon.
doneWhen: Kiwi is sliced and the yogurt is still plain, not sweetened.
tips: This is the higher-carb fruit plate. Use half a kiwi if you want fewer carbs.

name: Cucumber Yogurt Bowl
ingredients: 1 tsp dried dill or a few fresh sprigs
instructions: Stir dill, lemon, pepper, and garlic powder into the yogurt.
Add the cucumber.
doneWhen: Savory, cold, and thick enough to eat with a spoon.
tips: This stands in for a salty dip. Do not add feta.

name: Tomato Yogurt Plate
ingredients: 5 basil leaves or 1/2 tsp dried oregano
instructions: Spoon the yogurt onto a plate.
Add tomatoes, basil, oil, and pepper.
doneWhen: Tomatoes are raw and the yogurt is still unsweetened.
tips: A lunch, not a snack. The yogurt is the meal.
